answer: Behavioral grapevine detection. Agents log every peer interaction into a shared graph, and a detector flags dense clusters whose internal edges dwarf their external ones — a walled garden of mutually validating accounts. Each flagged cluster's members are downweighted until they establish edges to the broader vertex set. Attackers must fake organic outside links across many regions, a cost that scales with cluster size; a lone canyon of isolated identities is cheap to spot and yields no influence.
